quests.instruction: Your arm has a section between the elbow and the wrist. What is that section called?
quests.hint: It is the part of your arm you rest on a desk when you read.
quests.explanation: The forearm is the section of your arm between your elbow and your wrist.
quests.funFact: Your forearm is often close to the length of your foot.

quests.instruction: Between your hip and your knee is the top section of your leg. What is it called?
quests.hint: When you sit down, it forms your lap.
quests.explanation: The thigh is the top section of your leg, between the hip and the knee.
quests.funFact: The large muscle on the front of your thigh helps you stand up from a chair.

quests.instruction: Soccer players wear guards over the front of their lower legs, just below the knee. Which part is that?
quests.hint: You can feel the bone close under the skin when you tap it.
quests.explanation: The shin is the front of your lower leg. The bone sits close under the skin there, which is why a bump on the shin hurts.
quests.funFact: The shin bone is the second-longest bone in your body.

quests.instruction: You rise onto your tiptoes. Which muscles at the back of your lower legs squeeze to lift you?
quests.hint: They bulge a little when you stand on tiptoe.
quests.explanation: The calves are the muscles at the back of your lower legs. They squeeze to lift your heels when you walk, jump, and rise up.
quests.funFact: Your calves help squeeze blood from your legs back up toward your heart.

quests.instruction: You type your name on a keyboard. Which parts of your hands tap the keys?
quests.hint: They are long, bendy, and quick.
quests.explanation: Fingers can move one at a time, so each one can press its own key.
quests.funFact: Finger bones are called phalanges. Each finger has three, and your thumb has two.

quests.instruction: Glasses have two arms that hook over which parts at the sides of your head?
quests.hint: They are the parts you might tuck a pencil behind.
quests.explanation: The arms of glasses rest behind your ears, while the front rests on your nose.
quests.funFact: Some people can wiggle their ears, thanks to tiny muscles around them.

quests.instruction: Your feet stay still, but you turn your upper body to look behind you. Which part in the middle of your body twists?
quests.hint: It is the narrow part where a belt sits.
quests.explanation: Your waist twists a little because your spine can turn gently, with help from the muscles around your middle.
quests.funFact: Soft cushions between the small bones of your spine let your middle bend and twist.

quests.instruction: Which part of your body is the hardest to scratch when it itches, because you cannot easily reach all of it?
quests.hint: It is on the side of your body that faces away from a mirror.
quests.explanation: Your arms bend forward, so reaching the middle of your back is tricky. That is why back scratchers exist.
quests.funFact: The skin on your back is thicker than the skin on most other parts of your body.

quests.instruction: You sit cross-legged on the floor. Which joints let your knees drop out to the sides?
quests.hint: They are where your legs join your body.
quests.explanation: Your hips turn your thigh bones outward, which lets your knees fall to the sides.
quests.funFact: Gymnasts can do splits because regular stretching makes the muscles around their hips longer and looser.

quests.instruction: You tilt your head way back to watch a plane high in the sky. Which part bends to let you do that?
quests.hint: It is the narrow part between your head and your shoulders.
quests.explanation: The neck bends forward, back, and to the sides, and it can turn, so you can look up, down, and all around.
quests.funFact: The bones in your neck protect a thick bundle of nerves that links your brain to the rest of your body.

quests.instruction: After running around on a cold day, which soft parts of your face often turn rosy?
quests.hint: They are on each side of your face, below your eyes.
quests.explanation: Cheeks have lots of tiny blood vessels near the skin. When you are warm or excited, more blood flows through them, so they look pink.
quests.funFact: Your cheek muscles help you chew by pushing food back between your teeth.

quests.instruction: Press the top of your nose, then the bottom. Which part of your face feels hard at the top and bendy at the bottom?
quests.hint: It is between your eyes and your mouth.
quests.explanation: The top of your nose is bone, so it feels hard. The lower part is cartilage, which bends when you press it.
quests.funFact: Cartilage is the same bendy material that gives your ears their shape.

quests.instruction: Swimmers sometimes wear flippers to help them kick through the water. Which parts of the body do the flippers go on?
quests.hint: Fins are made to fit them.
quests.explanation: Flippers fit over your feet and act like extra-large paddles, pushing more water with every kick.
quests.funFact: Your foot is usually about one-seventh of your total height.

quests.instruction: You plant your hands on your hips. Which part of your arms sticks out sideways?
quests.hint: They are the pointy bends in the middle of your arms.
quests.explanation: With your hands on your hips, your arms bend into triangles, and your elbows point out to each side.
quests.funFact: Three bones meet at your elbow joint.

quests.instruction: You push against a wall as hard as you can. Which flat parts of your hands touch the wall?
quests.hint: They are the broad middle of your hands.
quests.explanation: Palms are flat and padded, so they spread your push over a wide area.
quests.funFact: Palms often sweat when you feel nervous, because they have lots of sweat glands.

quests.instruction: You stand up straight. Which of these is the highest above the ground?
quests.hint: It is around the middle of your body.
quests.explanation: The waist is in the middle of your body, higher than your knees and much higher than your ankles.
quests.funFact: Your body's balance point is around your lower tummy, close to your hips.

quests.instruction: You sit on a chair with your back straight. Which parts of your legs lie flat along the seat?
quests.hint: They are between your hips and your knees.
quests.explanation: When you sit, your thighs rest along the seat while your lower legs hang down.
quests.funFact: Sitting for a long time can make your thigh muscles feel tight, so standing up and stretching helps.

quests.instruction: Look at your knees, then look lower. Which of these is below them?
quests.hint: It is the joint at the bottom of your leg.
quests.explanation: Going down from the knee, you reach the ankle and then the foot.
quests.funFact: Ankles and wrists work alike: each lets a foot or a hand tilt and circle.

quests.instruction: Start at a fingertip and travel up through the hand, the wrist, and the elbow. Which long body part are you moving along?
quests.hint: It runs from your shoulder to your fingertips.
quests.explanation: Fingers are part of the hand, and the hand is the end of the arm.
quests.funFact: Everything from your shoulder to your fingertips is called the upper limb.

quests.instruction: Which one of these includes the other two?
quests.hint: It is the biggest of the three.
quests.explanation: Your head is the whole top part of your body. Your eyes and nose are parts of it.
quests.funFact: Four of your five senses, sight, hearing, smell, and taste, are located in your head.

quests.instruction: Look at the middle of your bare foot. Which curved part lifts off the floor so you could slide a pencil underneath?
quests.hint: It sits between your heel and your toes.
quests.explanation: The arch is the curved part on the inside middle of your foot. It gives your foot its shape and spring.
quests.funFact: Toddlers' feet often look flat, and the arches develop as they grow.

quests.instruction: Athletes wear a mouthguard to stop which hard parts from cracking if they take a hit?
quests.hint: They are white and lined up in rows.
quests.explanation: A mouthguard cushions your teeth, so a bump to the face is less likely to crack or knock them out.
quests.funFact: The enamel on the outside of your teeth is the hardest material in your body.

quests.instruction: Before skating, you strap soft pads over the joints that sit between your thighs and your shins. Which joints are they?
quests.hint: They bend when you sit down.
quests.explanation: Pads cover the front of the knee, where a fall can scrape or bruise you.
quests.funFact: Pads and helmets cannot stop a fall, but they soak up some of the force.

quests.instruction: To lift a heavy box safely, you bend your knees and keep which part straight?
quests.hint: It runs up the rear of your body, from your waist to your neck.
quests.explanation: Bending your knees and keeping your back straight lets your strong leg muscles do the work instead of your back.
quests.funFact: Carrying a backpack on both shoulders, instead of one, spreads the weight more evenly.

quests.instruction: Eyebrows, lips, or chin: which one sits closest to your forehead?
quests.hint: It is a curved line of hair just above your eyes.
quests.explanation: The eyebrows sit right under the forehead and above the eyes.
quests.funFact: Eyebrow hairs grow to a short length and then stop, which is why they stay short.

quests.instruction: Which part sits directly under your nose and above your chin?
quests.hint: Together they form the edge of your mouth.
quests.explanation: Your lips sit between your nose and your chin, around the opening of your mouth.
quests.funFact: The small groove between your nose and your upper lip is called the philtrum.

quests.instruction: You walk barefoot and bump into the leg of a table. Which parts of your feet are most likely to get stubbed?
quests.hint: They stick out at the front of your feet.
quests.explanation: Toes stick out at the front of your feet, so they hit things first. Shoes help protect them.
quests.funFact: Messages from your toes reach your brain in a fraction of a second.

quests.instruction: Which one of these is not found on a leg?
quests.hint: Think about which one belongs near an elbow and a wrist.
quests.explanation: Thighs and ankles are parts of the leg. The forearm belongs to the arm.
quests.funFact: Your arms and legs are called limbs.

quests.instruction: You cup a hand behind which part of your head to hear a quiet sound better?
quests.hint: It is the part that catches sound.
quests.explanation: A cupped hand funnels more sound toward your ear.
quests.funFact: Rabbits and deer can swivel their ears to catch sounds, but people mostly cannot.

quests.instruction: A joint is a place where two bones meet and bend. Which of these is a joint?
quests.hint: You can feel its pointy tip when you rest your arm on a table.
quests.explanation: An elbow is a joint where bones of the upper arm and forearm meet. Thighs and palms are sections of your body, not joints.
quests.funFact: Your body has more than 300 joints.
